evals.prompt: here are my notes from this week, they're a total mess. can you sort them out so i know what i owe people and what got decided? file is at <INPUT>/raw-standup-dump.md
evals.expected_output: Actionability-sorted markdown: diagnosis line, Actions (deduped incident-writeup TODO, owners kept, no invented dates), Decisions (usage-based tier, hold pricing page, 60-day EU notice), Ideas (trust page), Questions, Reference (EU p99 still degraded surfaced prominently), counts line that reconciles
assertions: Leads with a short diagnosis stating what the notes are and which organizing shape was chosen
All TODO/action items appear in an actions section, with the duplicate incident-writeup TODO merged to one entry
A Problems section exists and contains the EU latency regression (analyzer change never rolled back on EU cluster, p99 still degraded), cross-referenced to its action
A Wins section exists and contains the primary-cluster rollback fix (p99 back to 120ms) and/or Dana's confirmed 60-day answer
Decisions section contains: usage-based tier chosen (flat killed), hold pricing page until marketing signs off
No invented owners, dates, or facts (every owner/date in output traces to the input)
The trust-page idea (incl. uptime addition) is preserved in an ideas section, and the release-slip question is preserved
Ends with a counts line whose numbers reconcile

evals.prompt: i've been collecting these reading notes on learning science and they're just a pile. organize them into something i can actually build on as i read more. <INPUT>/reading-notes-learning.md
evals.expected_output: Concept-oriented atomic notes (retrieval practice, spacing, interleaving, desirable difficulties, storage-vs-retrieval strength, own-words elaboration), claim-like titles, sources merged per concept (Make It Stick + Karpicke on retrieval practice), links between related notes, index/MOC decision consistent with ~10-note threshold, counts reconcile
assertions: Notes are factored by CONCEPT, not by source (no 'Make It Stick notes' / 'Ahrens notes' section headers)
Retrieval practice note merges Make It Stick + Karpicke 2011 + Dunlosky under one concept with both/all sources cited
Note titles are claim-like statements (e.g. 'retrieval practice beats rereading'), not category labels
Related notes are explicitly linked (wikilinks or equivalent cross-references), incl. generation-effect connection the input flags with 'connects to the karpicke finding?'
Spacing note preserves the Cepeda 'gap scales with retention interval' claim with attribution
Storage strength vs retrieval strength (Bjork) is its own concept note
An index/MOC or linked list exists and is consistent with the skill's ~10-note threshold
Ends with a counts line whose numbers reconcile (incl. folded/merged source mentions)

evals.prompt: brain dump for an app idea, all over the place. turn it into one coherent doc i could show a friend. <INPUT>/brainstorm-sideproject.md
evals.expected_output: Single restructured doc: summary paragraph up top, themed sections (core concept, report freshness/expiry differentiator, cold start, revenue, MVP scope), duplicates merged, open questions section (liability, seed data legality), nothing dropped, counts reconcile
assertions: Single coherent document with a summary paragraph at the top
Ideas are clustered into named themes (concept/reports, freshness-expiry differentiator, cold start, revenue, MVP scope)
The report-expiry-by-type differentiator is given prominence matching the input's 'this is the differentiator' emphasis
The liability concern and seed-data legality (gray area) are preserved prominently (in an open-questions, risks, or equivalent section)
Rejected/parked items preserved (gamification doubt, offline maps rejected as scope creep, freshtracks name concern)
MVP decisions preserved faithfully: iOS only, 3 report types, Seattle (with reason), device-id no accounts
Nothing invented (no features, competitors, or numbers absent from input); ends with a reconciling counts line
